scope: Safe source-review exercises for the local HEVD copy. No build, no driver load, no device request, no payload and no exploit chain.

beginner.title: Orient yourself in the source tree
beginner.objective: Identify which files are driver source and which files are project metadata.
steps: Open research/hevd-source/SOURCE-ONLY.txt.
Open research/hevd-source/README.md and read the project purpose.
List the files under Driver/HEVD/Windows/ and note the .c and .h pairs.
Confirm that no upstream Exploit, Builder or installer Tools folder exists; the lowercase tools folder holds only the NetTruder helper.
beginner.evidence: A short note naming three source files and the safety boundary.
beginner.mitigation: Keeping exploit sources out of the lab copy makes the audit read-only by construction.

beginner.title: Run the first Code Audit
beginner.objective: Use NetTruder Code Audit on the HEVD source without executing anything.
steps: Open the CODE AUDIT module.
Press HEVD SOURCE to fill the path and start the read-only scan.
Wait for FILES WITH HITS and FINDINGS to populate.
Select a file with hits and read the masked source with line numbers.
beginner.evidence: The finding count and one masked snippet copied to your notes.
beginner.mitigation: Code Audit reads text only; no project is built and no driver is loaded.

beginner.title: Read one dangerous API finding
beginner.objective: Understand why a copy API is flagged without claiming exploitability.
steps: Open a finding with rule NT-C-DANGEROUS-COPY.
Read the masked line and the surrounding numbered source.
Write down what the destination size is and where it comes from.
Write a safe replacement using a bounded copy API.
beginner.evidence: A two-sentence defensive finding: risk, then fix.
beginner.mitigation: Bounded copies and length checks remove the class of bug being studied.

beginner.title: Send findings to RESEARCH
beginner.objective: Move masked Code Audit results into the RESEARCH module.
steps: Complete at least one Code Audit run.
Press SEND TO RESEARCH in the CODE AUDIT module.
Confirm the view switches to RESEARCH and FINDINGS increases.
Open one transferred finding and read its control and fix text.
beginner.evidence: The RESEARCH finding count before and after the transfer.
beginner.mitigation: The bridge carries masked text only; raw source is never sent.

beginner.title: Map a bug class to a catalog entry
beginner.objective: Connect one Code Audit rule to a HEVD catalog study entry.
steps: Open RESEARCH and filter the group to Kernel Source Review.
Find the entry that matches your finding, such as HEVD-COPY or HEVD-POOL.
Read DETECTION, HARDENING and EVENT CHAIN.
Record one control that reduces exposure to that bug class.
beginner.evidence: A note with rule ID, catalog ID, and one defensive control.
beginner.mitigation: Mapping findings to controls turns a code smell into an actionable review item.

beginner.title: Use the lab helper
beginner.objective: Generate a study guide and validate the local catalogs from the venv.
steps: Open a terminal in research/hevd-source.
Run .venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\hevd_lab.py check.
Run the same command with guide --level beginner.
Run findings to summarize the last Code Audit bridge file.
beginner.evidence: CHECK OK plus the generated guide heading.
beginner.mitigation: The helper reads local JSON and text only.

beginner.title: Read a wrapped-size finding
beginner.objective: Explain why arithmetic inside a bound check can make the check pass.
steps: Open HEVD-INT in RESEARCH and read DETECTION and HARDENING.
Run HEVD SOURCE in Code Audit and find an NT-C-INT-WRAP finding.
Read the masked line and name the arithmetic that feeds the comparison.
Write the checked-arithmetic fix and the maximum-size guard in your notes.
beginner.evidence: A short note with the rule ID, the arithmetic operation, and the documented fix.
beginner.mitigation: Checked arithmetic and a documented maximum stop a wrapped value from passing a bound check.

advanced.title: Build a data-flow review sheet
advanced.objective: Trace caller-controlled length values from the dispatch entry to the final copy.
steps: Open HEVD-IOCTL and HEVD-COPY in RESEARCH.
Mark each function in the path from dispatch to copy in your notes.
Record every length check and every arithmetic operation on that path.
Write a review sheet with source, bound, and destination capacity columns.
advanced.evidence: A table with three or more functions and one defensive conclusion.
advanced.mitigation: A complete data-flow sheet makes missing bounds visible without dynamic testing.

advanced.title: Audit allocation size arithmetic
advanced.objective: Review size calculations that feed kernel allocations.
steps: Open HEVD-POOL and HEVD-INT in RESEARCH.
Find an allocation size expression in the Windows source files.
Write the maximum possible value for each input using the documented types.
Propose a checked-arithmetic replacement and a maximum-size constant.
advanced.evidence: A written range analysis and the proposed guard.
advanced.mitigation: Checked arithmetic prevents undersized allocations before they happen.

advanced.title: Review object ownership
advanced.objective: Map allocation and free paths for one vulnerable-study object.
steps: Open HEVD-UAF in RESEARCH.
Mark allocation, reference, free and pointer-clear lines in the masked source view.
Write the single-owner rule that the code should follow.
Note one telemetry source that would show abnormal driver instability in a lab.
advanced.evidence: An ownership diagram in text form with four labelled steps.
advanced.mitigation: Reference counting and pointer clearing remove the lifetime ambiguity.

advanced.title: Review the user-pointer boundary
advanced.objective: Document the safe order for probe, copy, and validation.
steps: Open HEVD-PTR in RESEARCH.
Find a source file that accepts a caller-supplied pointer or buffer.
Record where probe, copy, exception handling and validation occur.
Write the single-snapshot pattern that should be used instead.
advanced.mitigation: Copying user data once into kernel-owned memory removes time-of-check gaps.

advanced.title: Write a custom Code Audit rule
advanced.objective: Add a defensive static rule for a bug class you studied.
steps: Pick one bug class from hevd-catalog.json.
Draft a regular expression that flags a narrow code pattern, not a whole file.
Add a rule with id NT-C-CUSTOM, severity, why, fix and a research tag.
Re-run Code Audit and verify the rule produces readable masked findings.
advanced.evidence: The rule text and one example finding title.
advanced.mitigation: Narrow, explainable rules reduce noise and keep the audit useful.

advanced.title: Produce a defensive research note
advanced.objective: Turn a set of findings into a beginner-friendly and advanced research note.
steps: Run the helper with guide --level all and save the output.
Select three Code Audit findings and transfer them to RESEARCH.
Write a short note with overview, evidence, controls, and limits.
State explicitly that no exploit was built, loaded or executed.
advanced.evidence: A Markdown note with four sections and a safety statement.
advanced.mitigation: Documenting evidence limits stops a source finding from being overstated.
